claims.statement: prefix: Fine-grained personal access tokens begin with the literal github_pat_.

sources.supports: Token-formats table lists github_pat_ as the fine-grained PAT prefix; it gives no length, alphabet, segment or checksum for it.

claims.statement: segments: After the prefix: 22 characters, one underscore, 59 characters (93 in total). (Recorded as community evidence with a staff endorsement. Kept visibly below the provider-documented prefix; the #223 hands-on checklist (93 total, one underscore at body offset 22) is human corroboration.)

sources.supports: Community gist: ^github_pat_[a-zA-Z0-9]{22}_[a-zA-Z0-9]{59}$. The product decision behind redact-secret#517 cites this gist and GitGuardian; the product implementation is therefore downstream of this community grammar, not independent evidence.

csine-pro 2022-10-19 proposed github_pat_[a-zA-Z-0-9]{22}_[a-zA-Z-0-9]{59} (the class admits a literal "-", probably a typo). hpsin (fine-grained PAT PM by content; authorAssociation NONE) replied 2022-10-24 "Your regex looks good" — a provider-staff endorsement in a community thread, not documentation.

claims.statement: body-length: The body after github_pat_ is 82 characters. (Three exact-82 tool rules (not independent of the community grammar they cite) against tolerant ranges (TruffleHog 36–255, r-lib/gh 36–244). No length twin is authored.)

sources.supports: gitleaks 8.30.1 github-fine-grained-pat: github_pat_\w{82} (no right boundary).
np.github.7: \b(github_pat_[0-9a-zA-Z_]{82})\b.
secretlint: (?<!\p{L})github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{82}(?![A-Za-z0-9_]).
trufflehog 3.97.4 github v2: (?:…|github_pat)_[a-zA-Z0-9_]{36,255} — a tolerant range, not a width claim.

claims.statement: alphabet: Each segment is [A-Za-z0-9]; the only underscore after the prefix is the separator. (Tools accept an underscore anywhere in the 82-character body (\w / [A-Za-z0-9_]). No fixture asserts silence on an underscore-shifted body; the separator twin uses ".", which no source admits.)

sources.supports: alphabet: Each segment is [A-Za-z0-9]; the only underscore after the prefix is the separator.
Provider changelog for the 2021 gh?_ scheme: [A-Za-z0-9_] and "up to 255 characters". It predates github_pat_ and names only the five gh?_ prefixes.

claims.statement: checksum: Whether the last characters of segment 2 carry a CRC32/Base62 checksum like the 2021 gh?_ scheme. (No checksum is claimed or computed; positives are random synthetic bodies.)

sources.supports: Documents CRC32/Base62 only for the 2021 gh?_ scheme.
Community claim that all GitHub v2 tokens carry a checksum; no provider source for github_pat_.
hpsin 2022-10-24: "purely a high-entropy string that's looked up on our backend" — denies embedded data, says nothing explicit about a checksum.

claims.statement: segment-1-lead: Whether segment 1 always begins "11". (Not claimed. Some positives start segment 1 with "11" and some do not, so no fixture depends on it either way.)

sources.supports: Anecdotal "github_pat_11AAAAAA0…" shape.
jasontempleman-eaton 2024-02-22 hypothetical masked display github_pat_11AS***.

claims.statement: ghes-parity: Whether GHES (GA from 3.17) issues the same github_pat_ shape.

sources.supports: GA; GHES expected in 3.17; token_id appears in API calls and audit logs. Format parity is not stated.
